newsitem.title: GERMANY: German wheat price improves with export sales.
newsitem.headline: German wheat price improves with export sales.

text.p: German wheat export prices have gained from European export trade demand, but the upside is limited by comfortable supplies, brokers said on Wednesday.
"Traders bought wheat for sales to southern Europe and third countries, including Uzbekistan," one said.
"But they won't tell you exactly where certain tonnages are aimed."
French exporters short of supplies to meet earlier orders were reported to be buyers in the German market at premiums.
The Hamburg grain exchange this week raised its bread wheat price (12.5 percent, 220 Hagberg) free Hamburg by 2.50 marks to 275 marks a tonne and the feed wheat price to 270, up five.
But three months of quiet conditions meant a lot of wheat was still stuck at cooperative or country merchant level and this supply was putting pressure on prices.
Operators were also aware that prices must not rise too sharply because this could discourage subsidy awards at the weekly EU export tender, traders said.
National ex-farm prices were at 245-260 marks, with farmers in characteristic export regions in the North asking for 250-255.

The premium of top qualities such as 14 percent protein over conventional wheat types had narrowed to less than 10 marks in the last three months and farmers were disappointed they had not achieved the prices they had hoped for, they said.
Farmers might consider sowing a smaller share of expensive seeds this autumn.
German export brokers were looking for 277.50-287.50 marks fob Baltic for first half March 12 percent wheat, while 13 and 14 percent material was offered at 285-302.50, depending on shipment sizes.
Fob barley sellers were steady at 260-275 marks and fob rye unchanged at 265-270.
